newsitem.title: JAPAN: Moody's leaves Yamaichi ratings, outlook negative.
newsitem.headline: Moody's leaves Yamaichi ratings, outlook negative.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Tuesday that it had confirmed the Baa3 and Prime-3 ratings for Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd's corporate debt and changed the ratings outlook to negative.
These actions conclude the review for a possible downgrade that was announced earlier in the year, Moody's said.

Moody's said that the rating confirmation reflects the progress achieved by Yamaichi in writing off its distressed real-estate loan portfolio, and in responding to challenges posed by the deregulating of Japan's financial markets.

Moreover, significant progress has been achieved by Yamaichi in reducing its expense base, and in eliminating overseas businesses that are not directly supporting its core domestic businesses, added Moody's.

Yamaichi achieved a 27 percent reduction in its overall expenses for the period covering fiscal years 1990 to 1997 -- the largest percentage expense cut by any of Japan's top four securities houses, Moody's said.
But Moody's added: "The foregoing progress notwithstanding, Yamaichi remains vulnerable to rapidly growing domestic competition."
